<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

All the three TEAEs reported in Phase 1 studies pool were mild in severity. No severe TEAEs were reported in Phase 2 studies pool, mild TEAEs were reported in five (10.4%) IPX203 subjects, and moderate TEAEs were reported in nine (18.8%) IPX203 subjects. In the Phase 3 studies pool, in AllIPX203 subjects, most of them experienced TEAEs that were either mild (163 [27.7%]) or moderate (174 [29.5%]) in severity; 60 (10.2%) subjects experienced severe TEAEs. The severe TEAEs reported by at least two IPX203 subjects were dyskinesia and nausea (4 [0.7%] subjects each), dry mouth (3 [0.5%]), and vomiting, volvulus, sepsis, fall, dizziness, syncope, sciatica, tremor, seizure, anxiety, depression, insomnia, nephrolithiasis, and hypertensive crisis (2 [0.3%] subjects each).

Of the 630 enrolled subjects, 365 (57.9%) experienced TEAEs: 289 (49.1%) who received IPX203 in total (i.e., IPX203 dose conversion period and IPX203 double-blind period combined) and 178 (28.3%) who received IR CD-LD in total (i.e., IR CD-LD dose adjustment period and IR CD-LD double-blind period combined). ## 5.5.3.1. Adverse Drug Reactions

In the Phase 1 studies pool, all three TEAEs reported in IPX203 subjects (i.e., vomiting, blood cholesterol increased, and dizziness) were considered treatment related.

In the Phase 2 studies pool, 10 (20.8%) IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs considered treatment related. The most commonly reported ( ≥ 5% subjects) treatment-related TEAEs in the IPX203 group were dyskinesia (six [12.5%] subjects) and dizziness (three [6.3%] subjects).

In the Phase 3 studies pool, 205 (34.8%) All-IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs considered treatment related. The most commonly reported ( ≥ 5% subjects) treatment-related TEAEs in the All-IPX203 group were dyskinesia (60 [10.2%] subjects) and nausea (32 [5.4%] subjects).

A comprehensive assessment of all AE PTs reported in the IPX203 Phase 2/3 studies was performed. The following factors were applied to determine which AEs would be considered ADRs:

- Frequency of the reported AE
- Whether or not the event was an ADR in the prescribing information for a similar product
- Whether or not the event was reported in the bibliographic reference studies
- Known pharmacologic class effects of dopaminergic drugs
- Severity and seriousness of the event
- Clinical importance of the event
- Whether or not the event could be considered a part of the natural history of PD
- Whether the event was considered secondary to another event (e.g., fractures secondary to a fall)
- Whether the event represented a subset of another AE or ADR term

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

The process was iterative, and the adjudicated designations reviewed to ensure consistency. Preferred Terms for AEs (e.g., acute psychosis, psychotic disorder, etc.) were grouped under a descriptive ADR term (e.g., psychotic episodes), and the ADR term assigned to an appropriate MedDRA SOC.

The incidence of each ADR was summarised by AE PT, ADR term and SOC, with each subject represented only once at each level.

In the proposed SmPC, each ADR has been categorised by frequency using standard categories: very common ( ≥ 1/10), common ( ≥ 1/100 to &lt;1/10), or uncommon ( ≥ 1/1,000 to &lt;1/100). Because fewer than 1000 subjects were included, no IPX203 ADRs have been categorised as rare ( ≥ 1/10,000 to &lt;1/1,000) or very rare (&lt;1/10,000).

In line with the recommendations outlined in the Guideline on SmPC, September 2009, only the Phase 3 controlled clinical trial IPX203-B16-02 has been considered to determine ADRs frequency, as considered sufficiently large to be informative.

Sixty-one ADRs were identified and summarised in the following Table.

Of note, the latest two Table's columns present:

- AE MedDRA PTs grouped and included in ADR term, collected during the controlled clinical study IPX203-B16-02 and considered to determine ADR frequency;
- Additional AEs PTs - covered by the same ADR term- collected from the remaining Phase 2 and 3 clinical trials and not considered for ADR frequency calculation.

The most frequently reported ADRs were dyskinesia (7.6%), nausea (6.6%), dry mouth (4.6%) and dizziness (4.2%).

## Adverse Events at Supratherapeutic Dose of carbidopa

In Study IPX203-101-23, no AEs were reported for any enrolled subject, and no clinically significant abnormal laboratory values were observed. Overall, 10 out of 35 (28.6%) subjects experienced at least one TEAE. Four (11.8%), 3 (9.1%), and one (2.9%) subject experienced at least one TEAE considered related to carbidopa, moxifloxacin hydrochloride, and placebo, respectively. The majority of TEAEs were mild in severity; no severe TEAE were reported. No TEAE led to discontinuation of the study drug, and no subject died or experienced other serious AEs. There were no clinically meaningful trends observed in haematology and chemistry parameters.

## Adverse Events by Average Total Daily Dose (TDD) and Total Cumulative Duration of Exposure

There was a higher systemic exposure of CD from IPX203. Therefore, this subsection discusses reported AEs according to CD exposure and total cumulative duration, determined based on the available IPX203 formulations with a 4:1 ratio of LD:CD at each IPX203 dosage strength. The TDD refers to the daily mg exposure to LD.

The most common TEAEs (defined as occurring in ≥5% subjects and in at least n=5 patients) were reported in the SOCs of Gastrointestinal, Infections and infestations, Injury, and Nervous System disorders . In each of the categories over time, &lt;1600 mg (CD &lt;400 mg) versus ≥1600 mg (CD ≥400 mg), the percentage of IPX203 subjects who experienced the most common TEAEs appeared stable over time. When comparing between dose categories over time (&lt;1600 mg versus ≥1600 mg), the percentage of IPX203 subjects who experienced the most common TEAEs were similar in ≥1600 mg versus &lt;1600 mg. Of note: = dyskinesia was generally lower in the higher dose category (≥1600 mg versus &lt;1600mg); this was observed consistently over time. Overall, the percentage of subjects with most common TEAEs was not unexpected and relatively stable over time and dose categories.

In the course of the procedure, the applicant was asked to discuss possible reasons for the higher incidence of TEAEs (including TEAEs related to study treatment) noted in subjects treated with IPX203 group compared to IR CD-LD in studies IPX203-B16-01 and IPX203-B16-02.

In the applicant's view, the higher incidence of TEAEs in study IPX203-B16-01 was as expected. In fact, the vast majority of TEAEs were dopaminergic side effects commonly associated with the use of LD. In this study patients had used levodopa therapy for years. They entered the study on the IR dose they had been stable on for long periods of time. IPX203 bioavailability was higher than originally anticipated by the applicant, and higher than often seen in MR preparations. Since the IR dose was usually established in patients by titrating until side effects emerged, it was expected that dopaminergic side effects would occur much more often in the IPX203 group, due to the study design. All TEAEs were considered mild or moderate. Six patients reported TEAEs during IPX203 treatment that were considered dopaminergic; most of these events resolved with a dose reduction.

In the IPX203-B16-02 study, patients were typically converted to IPX203-based on their current most frequent individual IR dose but with doses administered TID. Investigators rarely increased the dose frequency of IPX203 beyond TID; therefore, to increase the TDD individual doses were increased. The expected result of this increase in LD per administration event was an increase in dopaminergic side effects. One would expect this to increase the TEAE responses for IPX203 in both the dose titration and double-blind periods of the study.

Ultimately, it could be agreed that:

- In study IPX203-B16-01, the higher incidence of TEAEs in subjects treated with IPX203 group compared to IR CD-LD should be expected, since the study population had been using LD therapy for years. Thus, the higher incidence of TEAEs was most probably caused by IPX203 higher bioavailability. Nevertheless, it was reassuring that no severe TEAEs were observed.
- In study IPX203-B16-02, an increase in dopaminergic side effects was caused by increase in LD per administration.

## 5.5.5. Safety in special populations

The influence of the following intrinsic factors/subgroups on the AE profile of IPX203 was examined in the Phase 2 studies pool in advanced PD patients and in the Phase 3 studies pool in PD patients with motor fluctuations:

- Age: &lt;65, ≥65 years old at study entry
- Gender: Males, Females
- Race: Caucasians, non-Caucasians
- Region: North America, Europe
- Concomitant medications (please see section 5.4.8) - the following non-exclusive subgroups were defined for subjects taking concomitant medications of the following categories:
- Amantadine
- Selective MAO-B inhibitors
- Anticholinergic PD medications
- Dopamine agonists
- Others
- Weight: &lt;75 kg, ≥75 kg
- BMI: &lt;25 kg/m 2 , ≥25 kg/m 2
- PD duration at screening: &lt;8 years, ≥8 years
- Age of PD onset: &lt;65 years, ≥65 years

## Adverse Events by Age

In the Phase 2 studies pool, a higher percentage of ≥65 years -old IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs (50.0%) compared with &lt;65 years-old subjects (8.3%). In the Phase 3 studies pool, the TEAEs were comparable in &lt;65 years (67.7%) versus ≥65 years -old IPX203 subjects (67.2%). A higher percentage of ≥65 years IPX203 subjects experienced serious TEAEs (12.1%) versus &lt;65 years-old (7.1%), and a higher percentage of &lt;65 years IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs that led to discontinuation of the study drug (15.0%) versus ≥65 years -old (12.7%).

An overall summary of AEs by age groups, for the Phase 2 studies in advanced PD patients and for the Phase 3 Studies in PD Patients with motor fluctuations is presented (for the Safety Population) in the two Tables below.

In Phase 2 studies, a numerically higher proportion of IPX203 subjects aged ≥75 to &lt;85 years experienced TEAEs (50.0%) compared with those aged ≥65 to &lt;75 years (36.8%). Similar trends were observed also in the groups IR LDCD, and Rytary. No subjects ≥85 years old were enrolled in these studies.

One IPX203 subject ≥75&lt;85 (10.0%) experienced a serious TEAE ( Hypertension) and one a TEAE leading to discontinuation (10.0%) (Orthostatic hypertension).

In IPX203 ≥65&lt;75 years - old IPX203 subjects, the most commonly reported TEAE (≥5% and occurring in at least two subjects) was dyskinesia (21.1%).

In IPX203 ≥75&lt;85 years - old IPX203 subjects, the most commonly reported TEAE (≥5% and occurring in at least two subjects) was hypertension (20.0%).

A similar percentage of ≥75&lt;85 years -old IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs (68.4%) compared with ≥65&lt;75 years -old subjects (66.9%). Serious TEAEs were experienced by 12.6% of ≥75&lt; 85-year-old IPX203 subjects and 11.8% of ≥65&lt;75 years -olds. The percentage of TEAEs leading to discontinuation of study drug was 14.7% and 12.2%, respectively.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

In ≥65&lt;75 years - old IPX203 subjects, the most commonly reported TEAEs (≥5% and occurring in at least two subjects) were dyskinesia (10.3%), nausea (7.2%) and fall (5.3%).

In ≥75&lt;85 years - old IPX203 subjects, the most commonly reported TEAEs (≥5% and occurring in at least two subjects) were dyskinesia (9.5%), nausea (8.4%), constipation (5.3%), depression (5.3%), insomnia (5.3%), and fall (10.5%).

Overall, exposure in patients above 75 years is uncharacterised: no popPK analysis was conducted, and no PK was assessed in the Phase 3 studies. As experience with IPX203 in patients aged 75 years and older is limited (e.g. no patients above 85 have been enrolled in any IPX203 clinical trial), the SmPC (section 4.2, 4.4, 5.2) details that these patients should be converted cautiously from IR levodopa/DDCI into IPX203. Close clinical monitoring is recommended during the conversion period and subsequent dose optimisation, in line with standard clinical practice for older patients during dopaminergic therapy adjustments. Also of note, the dopaminergic adverse reactions these patients might be more susceptible to (outlined in SmPC section 4.4) include dyskinesia, hallucinations, confusion, somnolence, orthostatic hypotension, syncope and falls.

In the course of the procedure, based on the primary endpoint subgroup analysis (as discussed in Section 5.3.2.1), and with a close eye on safety-related matters, a careful evaluation of IPX203 treatment led to the following considerations in subjects (with):

- ≥65 years - The safety profiles were comparable across subgroups (TEAEs in ≥1 subject: 59.1% for onset &lt;65 years [n=470] versus 54.4% for onset ≥65 years [n=160]).
- body weight of &lt;75 kg - No evidence of reduced tolerability or excess AEs (that would contraindicate IPX203in lower � weight subjects) was noted.
- PD duration of ≥8 years - It is known that LD PK may be altered by gastrointestinal dysfunctions such as dysphagia, delayed gastric emptying, constipation, bacterial infection, gut dysbiosis, diet, comorbidities and concomitant medication intake (Leta et al , 2023). These factors may contribute to non-optimal LD response, symptoms fluctuations and unpredictable dyskinesia, and are more common in older patients and those with a PD onset in advanced age.
- PD onset at ≥65 years - The safety profiles were comparable across subgroups (TEAEs in ≥1 subject: 59.1% for onset &lt;65 years [n=470] vs 54.4% for onset ≥65 years [n=160]).
- 'Off' time of &lt;6 hours - The proportion of subjects with at least one TEAE was higher in subjects who reported 'OFF' time of ≥6 h (199 subjects out of 320, 62.2%) versus those who reported &lt;6 h at study entry (166 subjects out of 310; 53.5%). Thus, these data support the use of IPX203 in the overall population, without excluding patients with shorter baseline 'OFF' time.

In summary, the applicant adequately justified that safety was preserved across these patient's populations and no consistent signal of excess risk (that would warrant excluding these subgroups of patients from IPX203 treatment) was identified.

Furthermore, the safety profile of IPX203 was also confirmed as consistent across European and North America regions . The incidence of TEAEs was in favour of European subjects: in North America, 49.2% of IPX203 subjects and 32.8% of IR LD-CD subjects experienced a TEAE; in Europe, the rates were 35.8% and 30.2%, respectively. SAEs and discontinuations due to AEs were also

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

comparable, and no deaths were reported in either region.

There were some differences between the two regions in terms of:

- Severity of illness (14.9% of patients in North America and 29.3% in Europe were in HY stage 3-4),
- Duration of PD (7.72 years in North America, 8.84 years in Europe),
- Sex distribution (30.1% female in North America, 38.2% in Europe).

The applicant pointed out the article of Athulya et al (2020) reporting that age, disease duration, disease severity (Hoehn &amp; Yahr stage), duration of treatment with LD, TDD of LDD, and total LD equivalent dose were determinants of LD-induced dyskinesia. In the RISE-PD study, two of these predictors, i.e. higher severity and longer duration of PD, were more prevalent in the EU group. Another risk factor for developing dyskinesia is gender: the risk of dyskinesias is approximately three times higher in women compared to men (Cattaneo C., Pagonabarraga J. [2025]). The percentage of females was higher in the EU group compared to North America. Of note, all these differences between the two groups may have contributed to the lower 'Good ON' time observed in the European population.

## Renal disease

There are no published studies evaluating the PK of LD-CD in renally impaired patients. However, there is extensive clinical experience with LD-CD and review of the published literature has not highlighted or identified any significant safety concerns associated with use in renally impaired patients or those on haemodialysis. (Janzen et al 1999; Molnar et al 2006). In clinical practice, the dose of LD, generally, does not have to be adjusted in patients with renal failure.

The exact numbers of participants with mild and moderate renal impairment included in IPX203 clinical trials, and a summary of TEAEs and SAEs in these groups is detailed below.

An overall summary of AEs, by chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage, for both Phase 2 (in advanced PD patients) and Phase 3 studies (in PD patients with motor fluctuations) is presented below for the safety population.

## Phase 2 Studies

Overall, one subject in IPX2023 group (Stage 3a) experienced a non-serious related TEAE of dyskinesia.

## Phase 3 Studies - Stage 2 CKD

A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs (61.9%) as compared with those receiving IR LD-CD (41.7%). A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced related TEAEs (47.6%) as compared with those receiving IR LD-CD (16.7%). A lower percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced serious TEAEs (4.8%) as compared with those receiving IR LD-CD (8.3%) (see Table above).

One subject in the IPX203 group experienced serious TEAEs (dehydration, syncope, depression).

One subject in IPX203 group experienced a TEAE (Parkinson's disease) leading to drug discontinuation.

No TEAEs leading to death were reported.

In IPX203 subjects, the most commonly reported TEAE (≥5% and occurring in at least two subjects) were: dyskinesia (23.8%), dizziness (9.5%), neck pain (9.5%), nasopharyngitis (9.5%), restlessness (9.5%), dry mouth (9.5%), nausea (9.5%), and fall (9.5%).

## Phase 3 Studies - Stage 3a CKD

A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs (63.3%) as compared with those receiving IR LD-CD (21.9%). A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced related TEAEs (36.7%) as compared with those receiving IR LD-CD (6.3%). A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced serious TEAEs (6.7%) as compared with those receiving IR LD-CD (3.1%).

Two subjects in the IPX203 group experienced serious TEAEs (colitis, gastroenteritis viral, head injury, seizure, mental status changes). Five subjects in the IPX203 group experienced TEAEs leading to discontinuation (dyskinesia, freezing phenomenon, Parkinson's disease, seizure, nausea, head injury).

No TEAEs leading to death were reported.

In IPX203 subjects, the most commonly reported TEAE (≥5% and occurring in at least two subjects) were: dyskinesia (16.7%), nausea (10.0%), depression (10.0%), hallucination (6.7%), urinary tract infection (6.7%), fall (6.7%) (as outlined in the Tables below).

## Phase 3 Studies - Stage 3b CKD

A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced TEAEs (80.0%) as compared with IR LD-CD (45.5%) subjects. A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced treatment-related TEAEs

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

(40.0%) as compared with IR LD-CD (18.2%) subjects. A higher percentage of IPX203 subjects experienced serious TEAEs (20.0%) as compared with IR LD-CD (0.0%) subjects.

Two subjects in the IPX203 group experienced serious TEAEs (acute myocardial infarction, cardiac failure, concussion, confusional state). One subject in the IPX203 group experienced TEAEs (nausea, vomiting) leading to drug discontinuation. No TEAEs leading to death were reported.

In IPX203 subjects, the most commonly reported TEAEs (≥5% and occurring in at least two subjects) were: blood creatinine increased (20.0%), dyskinesia (30.0%), hypertension (20.0%), musculoskeletal pain (20.0%).

The numbers of participants with CKD enrolled in the Phase 3 studies are low, which limits the conclusions that can be drawn. Nevertheless, in the DB period of Study IPX203-B16-02, IPX203treated subjects with Stage 3a CKD showed higher rates of TEAEs (66.7% versus 16.7%) and treatment-related TEAEs (25.0% vs 0.0%) compared with IR LD-CD. Additionally, serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to discontinuation reported in IPX203-treated subjects with Stage 3a and Stage 3b CKD across the study warranted further attention. These findings were of concern also in the context of carbidopa notably excreted unchanged in urine and likewise considering that IPX203 produces approximately four-fold higher CD systemic exposure than IR LD-CD, providing a plausible mechanistic basis for excess toxicity in patients with impaired renal clearance.

Consequently, the applicant identified the specific TEAEs driving the higher rates of treatment-related TEAEs in Stage 3a/b CKD subjects during the DB period of Study IPX203-B16-02, and all serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to discontinuation across IPX203-treated subjects with Stage 3a/b CKD throughout the study.

For IPX203, all Serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to drug discontinuation were registered only during the dose conversion phase.

The serious TEAEs reported in the IPX203 group, in a total of four patients, were: colitis, concussion, head injury, confusional state, mental status changes, acute myocardial infarction, cardiac failure, gastroenteritis viral and seizure.

The TEAEs leading to drug discontinuation reported in the IPX203 group, in a total of six patients, were: dyskinesia, freezing phenomenon, Parkinson's disease, seizure, nausea, vomiting, head injury.

The serious events reported in Stage 3a/3b subjects include seizure, confusional state, mental status changes, acute myocardial infarction, cardiac failure, and bradycardia, which overlap with the profile the applicant attributed to high carbidopa exposure.

Carbidopa systemic exposure with IPX203 is approximately 4.5-fold that of IR LD-CD, and approximately 30% of carbidopa is excreted unchanged in urine with a further fraction eliminated renally as metabolites. In patients with reduced renal clearance, higher carbidopa exposure and the potential for accumulation are expected.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

All serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to discontinuation IPX203 subjects with stage 3a/3b (moderate) renal impairment occurred during the dose-conversion phase. The clustering of these events during such phase, before a stable dose is reached, indicates that the conversion step itself is the period of greatest risk in this population and that dose adjustment after conversion does not mitigate it. While the small number of stage 3a/3b subjects limits definitive conclusions, a relevant risk cannot be ruled out given the plausible mechanism. The potential effects of renal impairment on levodopa and carbidopa exposure are indirectly accounted for in dose titration. Nevertheless, dose adjustment should be conducted with caution in these special populations. Therefore, given the safety findings in stage 3a/3b subjects, higher carbidopa exposure, and its known renal excretion (as unchanged CD), the recommendations for appropriate clinical monitoring and caution on dose adjustment in the PI were extended from patients with severe renal impairment to those with moderate (renal) impairment (SmPC sections 4.2, 4.4, 5.2).

## Hepatic insufficiency

There are no published data to suggest that LD use in patients with hepatic disease is associated with significant safety concerns. Levodopa has been used in the treatment of hepatic encephalopathy (AlsNielsen et al 2004).

Overall, regarding hepatic impairment, the available sample is too small to draw meaningful conclusions. The applicant's proposed SmPC wording details that the potential effects of hepatic impairment on levodopa and carbidopa exposure are indirectly accounted for in dose titration (as referred to in sections 4.2, 4.4 and 5.2). Nevertheless, dose adjustment should be conducted with caution in patients with severe hepatic impairment, with appropriate clinical monitoring.

## 5.5.6. Immunological events

Not applicable.

## 5.5.7. Safety related to drug-drug interactions and other interactions

No drug-drug interaction (DDI) studies with IPX203 (LD-CD) have been performed. As with other LDCD-containing products, the use of nonselective MAO inhibitors with IPX203 is contraindicated. The use of selective MAO-B inhibitors (e.g., rasagiline and selegiline) with IPX203 may be associated with orthostatic hypotension. Dopamine D2 receptor antagonists (e.g., phenothiazines, butyrophenones, risperidone, metoclopramide) and isoniazid may reduce LD effectiveness. Iron salts or multi-vitamins containing iron salts can form chelates with LD and CD and cause a reduction in LD bioavailability from IPX203 (Sinemet SmPC 2023). The combination of different dopaminergic drugs may increase an

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

overall exposure to dopaminergic stimulation, some directly such as MAO-B inhibitors and some indirectly such as dopamine agonists.

## Adverse Events by use of concomitant medications

In the Phase 3 studies pool, the proportion of IPX203 subjects who experienced TEAEs were comparable with the concomitant use of dopamine agonists (67.3%, n=202), selective MAO-B inhibitors (65.8%, n=129), amantadine (65.9%, n=83), anticholinergic PD medications (62.5% n=15), and other medications (74.6%, n=85). Similar comparable results were reported for serious TEAEs with the concomitant use of dopamine agonists (10.0%, n=30), selective MAO-B inhibitors (10.7%, n=21), amantadine (7.9%, n=10), anticholinergic PD medications (12.5%, n=3), and other medications (11.4%, n=13).

Overall, TEAE rates, were broadly comparable across the available co-medication subgroups, and no clinically meaningful safety signal attributable to any specific co-medication class was identified.

In Study IPX203-102-23, the estimated slope of carbidopa plasma concentration in the concentrationQTc relationship was extremely shallow and not statistically significant: -0.00020 ms per ng/mL (90% CI: -0.001644 to 0.001237; P = 0.8141) with a very small and not statistically significant treatment effect-specific intercept of 0.75 ms. The effect on ΔΔ QTcF can be predicted to 0.48 ms (90% CI: -1.00 to 1.97) at the geometric mean peak concentration for the carbidopa 400 mg dose (1333.8 ng/mL). Based on this concentration-QTc analysis, a QTcF effect ( ΔΔ QTcF) exceeding 10 ms could be excluded within the full observed plasma concentrations of CD up to approximately 3000 ng/mL.

## 5.5.9. Post-marketing experience

IPX203 was approved in the US [via the 505(b)(2) pathway] on 7 August 2024 and launched in September 2024 under the brand name Crexont. In accordance with information available in the Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report(s) (PADERs) no new safety concerns has been observed for IPX203.

## 5.5.10. In vitro biomarker test for patient selection for safety

Not applicable.

## 5.5.11. Overall discussion and conclusions on clinical safety

## 5.5.11.1. Discussion

## 5.5.11.1.1. Overall assessment of available safety data

The clinical safety evaluation of IPX203 is based on seven clinical studies : two early phase PK and bioavailability trials in healthy volunteers, two supportive Phase 2 studies (Study IPX203-B14-02 and Study IPX203-B16-01) in patients with Parkinson's disease, and the pivotal randomised, double-blind, active-controlled Phase 3 trial with its 9-month open-label extension 3 (Study IPX203-B16-02 and Study IPX203-B16-03, respectively). Additionally, two Phase 1 studies were conducted with carbidopa alone to further assess the safety and tolerability of its high doses, considering the higher systemic exposure observed with IPX203 compared with immediate-release LD/CD.

The safety database is of sufficient size, and the FU adequate for IPX203 intended use, and considering the long clinical experience with levodopa/carbidopa fixed-dose combination medicinal products in the (EU) market. In total, 731 participants received IPX203, 589 of which in the pivotal Phase 3 trial and its open-label extension in PD patients with motor fluctuations, which provided the main body of safety data.

In Study IPX203-B14-02 , out of the 26 enrolled subjects, nine (34.6%) reported at least one TEAE. However, there were no deaths, SAEs or AEs that led to premature discontinuation. TEAEs were reported by more subjects during IR CD-LD (7/25; 28.0%) and IPX203 (5/26; 19.2%) treatments than during Rytary (2/25; 8.0%) treatment. The majority of TEAEs were mild, and none classified as severe. TEAEs reported by t or more subjects included dizziness (3 subjects), nausea (2), and hypertension (2).

In Study IPX203-B16-01 , out of the 28 enrolled subjects, 11 (39.3%) reported TEAEs. A higher percentage reported TEAE(s) while taking IPX203 (10; 35.7%) than IR CD-LD (2; 7.4%). The incidence of reported TEAEs considered related to the study treatment was also higher in subjects receiving IPX203 than IR CD-LD (8 versus 1, respectively).

All reported TEAEs were assessed as mild or moderate. No severe TEAEs were reported. However, in IPX203 group seven subjects (25%) had one or more TEAEs with a maximal severity of mild and seven (25%) with a maximal severity of moderate. In IR CD-LD group, the number of subjects was much lower: two subjects (7.4%) had one or more TEAEs with maximal severity of mild, and one (3.7%) had one or more TEAEs with maximal severity of moderate.

One IPX203 subject experienced a treatment-emergent SAE (increased hypertension), assessed as not related to the treatment. Moreover, one subject experienced three SAEs (moderate dehydration, severe diarrhoea, and moderate atrial fibrillation) during the washout period, starting seven days after completing IPX203 treatment. One subject was withdrawn from the study due to intermittent moderate orthostatic hypertension. TEAEs reported by two or more subjects included dyskinesia (5 subjects), dizziness (2), and nausea (2); all these TEAEs occurred during IPX203 treatment. All other TEAEs occurred in a single subject each. Six subjects reported dopaminergic TEAEs during IPX203 treatment period; most of these events resolved with a dose reduction.

The applicant discussed possible reasons for the higher incidence of TEAEs (including those related to study treatment) in subjects receiving IPX203. Such higher incidence would be expected in a study population which had been using LD therapy for years and most probably caused by IPX203 higher bioavailability. This justification was considered acceptable.

In the pivotal Study IPX203-B16-02 , 506 subjects were included in the Safety Analysis Set (SAS).

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Overall, of the 630 enrolled, 57.9% experienced TEAEs: 49.1% who received IPX203 and 28.3% who received IR CD-LD. Thirty (4.8%) subjects experienced SAEs and 62 (9.8%) discontinued the study drug due to TEAEs. No deaths occurred during this study. During the dose adjustment period, higher number of subjects reported TEAEs in IPX203 group compared to IR CD-LD group. In IR CD-LD group, 118 (18.7%) subjects experienced TEAEs, including 31 (4.9%) treatment-related TEAEs. Six (1.0%) experienced TEAEs that led to discontinuation of the study drug and 7 (1.1%) experienced serious TEAEs. In IPX203 group 229 (38.9%) subjects experienced TEAEs, including 140 (23.8%) treatmentrelated TEAEs. Forty-two (7.1%) subjects experienced TEAEs that led to discontinuation of the study drug and 12 (2.0%) experienced serious TEAEs.

During the double-blind (DB) period, the number of TEAEs was higher in subjects receiving IPX203 (108 [42.2%]) compared with those receiving IR CD-LD (79 [31.6%]). Forty-two (16.4%) subjects who received IPX203 and 17 (6.8%) who received IR CD-LD experienced treatment-related TEAEs. Fourteen (5.5%) IPX203 subjects and 3 (1.2%) IR CD-LD ones experienced TEAEs that led to discontinuation of the study drug. Eight (3.1%) IPX203 subjects and 4 (1.6%) IR CD-LD subjects experienced serious TEAEs. Of note, during the DB period, 11 (4.3%) subjects in IPX203 group reported nausea, compared to 2 (0.8%) in IR CD-LD group. Moreover, dizziness was reported by six (2.3%) subjects in IPX203 group, compared to two (0.8%) in IR CD-LD group. Furthermore, seven subjects (2.7%) in IPX203 group reported anxiety, compared to zero subjects in IR CD-LD group.

The overall proportion of subjects who experienced at least one TEAE was higher in &lt;65-year-old subjects (61.4%, n=236) versus those ≥65 -year-old (55.8%, n=394). However, during the DB period there were no relevant differences in these percentages in both treatment groups in terms of TEAEs (IPX203: 44.0% versus 41.0% and IR CD-LD: 30.4% versus 32.3%, respectively). Similarly, there were no obvious differences in percentages of males and females who experienced TEAEs (57.8% versus 58.1%, respectively).

A higher proportion of subjects in North America (60.9%, n=327) experienced at least one TEAEs compared to European subjects (54.8%, n=303). However, the difference during the DB period was more pronounced in IPX203 group (49.2% versus 35.8%) compared to IR CD-LD group (32.8% versus 30.2%).

During the DB period, there were small differences in the percentage of subjects who experienced TEAEs between those with PD onset at ≥65 years and the ones with PD onset at &lt;65 years (46.8% versus 40.7%, respectively in the IPX203 group and 32.6% versus 28.8%, respectively in the IR CD-LD group).

The most frequently reported TEAEs ( ≥ 2%) in subjects from IPX203 group were dyskinesia (45 [7.6%]), nausea (39 [6.6%]), dry mouth (27 [4.6%]), dizziness (23 [3.9%]), fall (17 [2.9%]), vomiting (16 [2.7%]), constipation, anxiety, insomnia (15 [2.5%)] subjects each), and headache (12 [2.0%]).

The most frequently reported TEAE ( ≥ 2%) in subjects who received IR CD-LD was fall (15 [2.4%]).

During the DB period, TEAEs were reported in 108 (42.2%) subjects who received IPX203 and in 79 (31.6%) who received IR CD-LD. The most frequently reported TEAEs ( ≥ 2%) in subjects who received IPX203 were nausea (11 [4.3%]), anxiety (7 [2.7%]), dizziness (6 [2.3%]), and dyskinesia and fall (each 5 [2.0%]). The most frequently reported TEAEs ( ≥ 2%) in subjects who received IR CD-LD were fall (9 [3.6%]), urinary tract infection (8 [3.2%]).

The majority of subjects experienced TEAEs that were either mild (171 [27.1%]) or moderate (156 [24.8%]) in severity; 38 (6.0%) subjects experienced severe TEAEs (4.4% on IPX203 total and 2.1% on IR CD-LD total).

During the DB period, eight (3.1%) subjects in IPX203 group and seven (2.8%) in IR CD-LD experienced severe TEAEs. The severe TEAEs in the IPX203 group were anxiety, feeling abnormal, nausea, dizziness, dysesthesia, mixed hallucinations, and sciatica (each in one [0.4%] subject), and hypoesthesia and pain in extremity (in one [0.4%] subject). In those receiving IPX203, the time to resolution varied depending on the event type. Nevertheless, overall, the duration of events is not considered different from what would be expected.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

The severe TEAEs experienced by subjects in IR CD-LD group were: atrioventricular block complete, asthenia, PD, mass, fatigue, back pain (each in one [0.4%] subject), and sciatica and limb injury (in one [0.4%] subject).

A total of 188 (29.8%) subjects experienced TEAEs considered treatment-related: 165 (28.0%) who received IPX203 in total (i.e., IPX203 dose conversion period and IPX203 DB period combined) and 47 (7.5%) who received IR CD-LD in total (i.e., IR CD-LD dose adjustment period and IR CD-LD DB period combined). Compared to IR CD-LD group, a higher number of subjects with treatment-related TEAEs was noted in IPX203 group.

During the DB period, 42 (16.4%) subjects in IPX203 group and 17 (6.8%) in IR CD-LD group experienced treatment-related TEAEs. The most frequently reported ones ( ≥ 1%) experienced by IPX203 group subjects were nausea (7 [2.7%]), dyskinesia (5 [2.0%]), and feeling abnormal and fall (3 [1.2%] subjects each). The treatment-related TEAEs in the IR CD-LD group were noted in less than 1% of subjects.

Thirty (4.8%) subjects experienced serious TEAEs; 20 (3.4%) who received IPX203 and 10 (1.6%) who received IR CD-LD. Moreover, 62 (9.8%) experienced TEAEs that led to study drug discontinuation; 55 (9.3%) receiving IPX203 and 9 (1.4%) receiving IR CD-LD.

It can be agreed that no new, emerging safety issues have been reported in IPX203 - exposed subjects. Nevertheless, higher incidence of TEAEs (including treatment-related TEAEs) was noted. In this study, patients were typically converted to IPX203-based on their current most frequent individual IR dose, but with doses administered three times a day (TID). Investigators rarely increased the dose frequency of IPX203 beyond TID. Therefore, to increase the TDD, individual doses were increased. The expected result of this increase in LD per administration was an increase in dopaminergic side effects. One would expect this to increase the TEAE responses for IPX203 in both the dose titration and DB periods of the study. This justification (that an increase in dopaminergic side effects had been caused by increase in LD per administration) was endorsed.

Furthermore, based on the primary endpoint subgroup analysis (as discussed in Section 5.3.2.1), and with a close eye on safety-related matters, the applicant evaluated accurately IPX203 treatment in subjects (with):

## · ≥65 years

Safety profiles were comparable across subgroups (TEAEs in ≥1 subject: 59.1% for onset &lt;65 years [n=470] versus 54.4% for onset ≥65 years [n=160]).

## · body weight of &lt;75 kg

No evidence of reduced tolerability or excess AEs (that would contraindicate IPX203in lower � weight subjects) was confirmed.

## · PD duration of ≥8 years

It is known that LD PK may be altered by gastrointestinal dysfunctions such as dysphagia, delayed gastric emptying, constipation, bacterial infection, gut dysbiosis, diet, comorbidities and concomitant medication intake (Leta et al , 2023). These factors may contribute to non-optimal LD response, symptoms fluctuations and unpredictable dyskinesia, and are more common in older patients and those with a PD onset in advanced age.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## · PD onset at ≥65 years

Safety profiles were comparable across subgroups (TEAEs in ≥1 subject: 59.1% for onset &lt;65 years [n=470] vs 54.4% for onset ≥65 years [n=160]).

## · 'Off' time of &lt;6 hours

The proportion of subjects with at least one TEAE was higher in subjects who reported 'OFF time' of ≥6 h (199 subjects out of 320, 62.2%) versus those who reported &lt;6 h at study entry (166 subjects out of 310; 53.5%). Thus, these data support the use of IPX203 in the overall population, without excluding patients with shorter baseline 'OFF time'.

In summary, it was adequately justified that safety was preserved across the patient populations above listed and no consistent signal of excess risk was identified that would warrant excluding these subgroups of patients from IPX203 treatment.

In the OLE Study IPX203-B16-03 a total of 419 enrolled subjects were included in the SAS. Overall, the 52.7% experienced TEAEs: 51.5% from the previous IPX203 group and 54.0% from the previous IR CDLD group.  A total of 66 (15.8%) subjects experienced treatment-related TEAEs; 25 (6.0%) TEAEs led to discontinuation of the study drug and 42 (10.0%) were serious TEAEs. Six subjects died during this study.The most frequently reported TEAEs in both groups were dyskinesia, fall and urinary tract infection (21 [5.0%]), back pain (15 [3.6%]) and constipation (11 [2.6%]). These TEAE can be considered wellknown safety issues of CD-LD. The majority of subjects experienced TEAEs that were either mild (107 [25.5%]) or moderate (77 [18.4%]) in severity; 37 (8.8%) experienced severe TEAEs. In total, three severe TEAEs of volvulus, fall, and seizure were reported in two (0.5%) subjects each, while the remaining severe TEAEs were reported in one (0.2%) subject each.

Sixty-six (15.8%) subjects experienced treatment-related TEAEs and the most frequently reported ones were dyskinesia (19 [4.5%] subjects) and nausea (4 [1.0%]).

Subjects aged ≥65 years experienced higher rates of both TEAEs (55.8% vs 47.4%) and SAEs (12.0% vs 6.6%) compared to those under 65 . Urinary tract infections (6.7% vs 2.0%), falls (6.4% vs 2.6%), and hallucinations (3.0% vs 0%) were more frequently reported by subjects aged ≥65 years than by those under 65 .

The incidence of TEAEs and SAEs was comparable between subjects with a PD duration of &lt;8 years (55.4% and 10.2%, respectively) and those with a duration of ≥8 years (50.6% and 9.9%, respectively.

The incidence of dyskinesia was higher in subjects with a PD duration of ≥8 years than in those with &lt;8 years (6.4% vs 3.2%). The AEs experienced by 32 (7.6%) subjects enrolled in Study IPX203-B16-02 were resolved only after entering the OLE Study IPX203-B16-03: 20 (4.8%) of the resolved TEAEs included constipation [3 subjects]; radius fracture, weight decreased, decreased appetite, back pain, insomnia [2 subjects each] andthe remaining were in 1 subject each.

However, in 112 (26.7%) subjects the AEs were not resolved. These included dry mouth (14 subjects); dyskinesia (9; orthostatic hypotension (7); fatigue, somnolence, depression, hypertension (6 subjects each); constipation, back pain (5 subjects each); dyspepsia, hallucination, visual (4 subjects each); blood pressure increased, arthralgia, pain in extremity, anxiety, insomnia, headache (3 subjects each); atrial fibrillation, vision blurred, pain, decreased appetite, arthritis, muscle spasms, musculoskeletal pain, neck pain, balance disorder, carpal tunnel syndrome, cognitive disorder, freezing phenomenon, hypoaesthesia, affect lability, asthma, hypotension (2 subjects each) and the remaining were in one subject each. Six subjects died during the OLE study. Five of these deaths were unrelated to the study drug; the remaining case was a severe SAE of drowning considered related to IPX20. Other deaths were caused by subarachnoid haemorrhage, cardiogenic shock, pulmonary embolism, volvulus and sepsis. Forty-two (10.0%) subjects experienced serious TEAEs. The most commonly reported TEAEs were COVID-19, seizure, and confusional state (each in three subjects), and atrial fibrillation, volvulus, pneumonia, femur fracture, syncope, psychotic disorder, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and pulmonary embolism (each in two subjects). All of these serious TEAEs were assessed as not related to the study drug, except for fall, polyneuropathy, hypersensitivity, psychotic disorder, overdose, drowning, and pyrexia and delirium. Six serious TEAEs were fatal. Four serious TEAEs were not recovered/not resolved prior to study end: scoliosis, colitis, delirium, and cauda equina syndrome. Overall, the AE profile observed across IPX203 development programme is largely consistent with the known safety profile from other LD/CD formulations. The most common ADRs were dyskinesia, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness. The distribution of events between treatment groups was broadly comparable. Analyses of SAEs and AEs leading to drug discontinuation did not raise new or unexpected safety concerns compared to other LD/CD products. Furthermore, the subgroup analyses did not reveal new, emerging safety concerns. Special attention was paid to IPX203 administration in case of renal impairment. Subjects with stage 3a/3b chronic kidney disease (CKD) had higher rates of treatment-related TEAEs with IPX203 than with IR LD-CD. All serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to discontinuation in IPX203-treated Stage 3a/3b subjects occurred during the dose-conversion phase. Carbidopa systemic exposure with IPX203 is approximately 4.5-fold that of IR LD-CD, and approximately 30% of CD is excreted unchanged in urine, with a further fraction eliminated renally as metabolites. Therefore, higher exposure and accumulation are expected with reduced renal clearance. The SAEs reported in these subjects including seizure, confusional state, mental status changes, acute myocardial infarction, cardiac failure, and bradycardia, overlap with the profile the applicant itself attributes to high carbidopa exposure.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

All serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to discontinuation of IPX203 in subjects with stage 3a/3b (moderate) renal impairment occurred during the dose-conversion phase. The clustering of these events in this phase, before a stable dose is reached, indicates that the conversion step itself is the period of greatest risk in this special population and that dose adjustment after conversion does not mitigate it. While the small number of stage 3a/3b subjects limits definitive conclusions, a relevant risk cannot be ruled out, given the plausible mechanism. The potential effects of renal impairment on levodopa and carbidopa exposure are indirectly accounted for in dose titration. Nevertheless, dose adjustment should be conducted with caution in 3a/3b CKD subjects. Thus, given these safety findings, recommendations for appropriate clinical monitoring and caution on dose adjustment for patients with moderate to severe renal impairment are outlined in the PI. With regard to the elderly population, in the DB period of study IPX203-B16-02, older subjects, particularly those aged ≥75 to &lt;85 years treated with IPX203 showed higher rates of treatment -related TEAEs (22.9% versus 6.7%), serious TEAEs (11.4% versus 2.2%), and TEAEs leading to discontinuation (11.4% versus 4.4%) as compared with IR LD-CD. The applicant identified the contributing events, which were predominantly dopaminergic, along with serious cases of epilepsy and bradycardia. Exposure above 75 years is uncharacterised: no popPK analysis was conducted, and no PK was assessed in the Phase 3 studies. Therefore, as experience with IPX203 in patients aged 75 years and older is limited (e.g., no patients above 85 have been enrolled in any IPX203 clinical trial), the SmPC (section 4.2, 4.4, 5.2) details that these patients should be converted cautiously from IR levodopa/DDCI into IPX203. Close clinical monitoring is recommended during the conversion period and subsequent dose optimisation, in line with standard clinical practice for older patients during dopaminergic therapy adjustments. Also of note, the dopaminergic ADRs these patients might be more susceptible to (outlined in SmPC section 4.4) include dyskinesia, hallucinations, confusion, somnolence, orthostatic hypotension, syncope and falls. In addition, the safety profile of IPX203 was consistent across both European and North American regions. Concerning TEAEs incidence: in North America 49.2% of IPX203 and 32.8% of IR LD-CD subjects experienced a TEAE, respectively; in Europe, the rates were 35.8% and 30.2%, respectively. SAEs and discontinuations due to AEs were also comparable. No deaths were reported in either region. There were some differences between the two regions in terms of:

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

- Severity of illness (14.9% of patients in North America and 29.3% in Europe were in HY stage 3-4),
- Duration of PD (7.72 years in North America, 8.84 years in Europe),
- Sex distribution (30.1% female in North America, 38.2% in Europe).

Athulya et al (2020) reported that age, disease duration and severity (Hoehn &amp; Yahr stage), duration of treatment with LD, TDD of LDD, and total LD equivalent dose were determinants of LD-induced dyskinesia. In the pivotal trial, two of these predictors, i.e., higher severity and longer duration of PD, were more prevalent in the EU group. Another risk factor for developing dyskinesia is gender: the risk is approximately three times higher in women compared to men (Cattaneo C., Pagonabarraga J. [2025]). The percentage of females was higher in the EU group compared to the North American one. All these differences may have contributed to the lower 'Good ON' time observed in the European population.

No relevant safety signals were seen in laboratory tests or vital signs. Abnormal ECG values and ECGrelated TEAEs were low and similar to IR LD/CD overall. In the TQT study, AEs were infrequent and mostly mild and carbidopa showed no exposure-response effect on QTc, supporting no meaningful QT prolongation at therapeutic and high CD exposures.

The overall methodology used to define ADRs in the SmPC is also acceptable.

## 5.5.11.1.2. Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in the SmPC

The ADRs proposed by the applicant for inclusion in the SmPC, as described above, are overall acceptable.

Furthermore, as triggered by the PRAC recommendation for CMDh attention pertaining to EMA/PSUR/0000327864 for carbidopa / levodopa (NAP), also applicable to Hopledo, the following ADR should be included in the SmPC (and PL, accordingly).

|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|

In addition, the CHMP agreed that the text below, also recommended by PRAC to CMDh in the framework of procedure EMA/PSUR/0000327864, should be included in SmPC section 4.4 (and PL, accordingly), to complement the update of SmPC section 4.8, as noted above:

- ' Treatment with carbidopa/levodopa can lead to vitamin B6 deficiency, which may increase the risk of seizures, particularly in patients receiving higher doses, and/or those with poor nutritional status. Monitoring of pyridoxine (vitamin B6) levels and vitamin B6 supplementation should be considered in patients receiving high-dose carbidopa/levodopa and those presenting with clinical manifestations suggestive of vitamin B6 deficiency ' .

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## 5.5.11.2. Conclusions on clinical safety

The safety profile of IPX203 is acceptable and consistent with the long-standing clinical experience with levodopa/carbidopa. The PI reflects accordingly the need for dose adjustment and/or careful clinical monitoring in patients with (moderate to severe) renal or (severe) hepatic impairment. Furthermore, it details that elderly patients should be converted cautiously from immediate-release levodopa/DDCI. Close clinical monitoring is also recommended during the conversion period and subsequent dose optimisation, in line with standard clinical practice for older patients during dopaminergic therapy adjustments, as they would be more susceptible to dopaminergic adverse reactions.

## 7. Pharmacovigilance

## 7.1. Pharmacovigilance system

The CHMP considers that the pharmacovigilance system summary submitted by the applicant fulfils the requirements of Article 8(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC.

## 7.2. Periodic safety update reports (PSURs) submission requirements

The requirements for submission of periodic safety update reports for this medicinal product are set out in the list of Union reference dates (EURD list) provided for under Article 107c(7) of Directive 2001/83/EC and any subsequent updates published on the European medicines' web-portal.

The CHMP considered that (e.g. regarding therapeutic indication, posology, pharmaceutical form) Hopledo does not differ significantly from the already approved medicinal products containing carbidopa/levodopa. Therefore, it should be added to the existing entry in the EURD list for carbidopa/levodopa (NAP) fixed-dose combination and follow a 3-year PSUR cycle. Hopledo first PSUR data lock point (DLP) will be 1 October 2028.

## 8. Product information

## 8.1. Summary of product characteristics (SmPC)

## 8.1.1. SmPC section 4.1 justification

The wording of the indication has been agreed to be as follows:

- Hopledo is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with Parkinson's disease and moderate to severe motor fluctuations who have not been sufficiently stabilised with oral levodopa/dopa decarboxylase (DDC) inhibitor based treatment regimens.

The applicant's initially proposed text (detailed below) was not considered adequate by CHMP:

- Hopledo® is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with Parkinson's disease and moderate to severe motor fluctuations who cannot be stabilised on levodopa/dopa decarboxylase (DDC) inhibitor treatment and/or other available Parkinson oral medicinal products.

It appeared contradictory to state that Hopledo, with its mix of oral IR and PR levodopa/carbidopa, should be indicated for PD patients ' who cannot be stabilised' on oral medications (i.e., in line with the approved products for continuous infusions via the duodenal or subcutaneous routes) since this medicinal product indeed is an[other] oral Parkinson's disease medication.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

The CHMP expressed that the modest improvement of 'Good on time' and 'OFF time' could not be considered to make the difference between 'stabilisation' and 'non-stabilisation' of PD for the proposed target population.

Thereafter, the applicant justified the modest statistical effect of IPX203 over the MR / IR levodopa with the complex study design and strict titration rules and timings, which were acknowledged by CHMP. Notwithstanding, the benefit, as shown in the study conditions, is considered scarce in clinical terms. While this population mean benefit is small, it may, nonetheless, be relevant to the individual patients, along with the better convenience of three intakes per day. The latter was considered an advantage by CHMP, especially for elderly patients with moderate-severe motor fluctuations and/or those who cannot handle infusion pumps or are not eligible for deep brain stimulation (DBS) treatment.

Also, of note: in the course of the procedure, the applicant provided analyses in various subpopulations, looking at different stages of disease severity (e.g., less or more than 6 hours 'OFF time' at baseline), with long 'OFF time' duration, observing that the effect size is preserved in all disease's states.

The user test for Hopledo was performed by 'Knowhownow'. The key outcomes of this test are listed below:

- Overall, the test methodology was considered acceptable;
- The inclusion and exclusion criteria for the recruitment were well described;
- The key safety issues were appropriately targeted through the questionnaire, reflecting the safe and correct use of the medicinal product:

## 9. Benefit-risk assessment

## 9.1. Therapeutic context

## 9.1.1. Disease or condition, proposed therapeutic indication

Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder. The prevalence is increasing, both due to ageing of the population and other non-identified causes. According to the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, the global prevalence of PD was estimated at 138.6/100,000 people and caused 388,000 deaths in the world population. By 2035, age-standardised rates of incidence and prevalence will increase from 14.62/100,000 and 139.79/100,000, noted in 2021, to 20.20/100,000 and 165.05/100,000, respectively (Luo et al 2025). In Europe, in a projection between 2021 and 2050, the all-age prevalence of PD was estimated between 152/100,000 and 267/100,000, respectively (Su et al 2025).

The early stages of the disease are mostly well controlled with the available medications, but when the patient develops motor fluctuations, the control of the disease becomes a challenge.

Hopledo is proposed for the treatment of adult PD patients with moderate to severe motor fluctuations who have not been sufficiently stabilised with oral levodopa/dopa decarboxylase (DDC) inhibitor-based treatment regimens.

## 9.1.2. Available therapies and unmet medical need

Levodopa (LD), in combination with carbidopa (CD), is considered an efficacious treatment for the motor symptoms of PD, and nearly all PD patients require LD treatment as the disease progresses (Jankovic and Poewe 2012). Despite the available treatment options, including adjunctive therapies and rescue medications, disease progression and LD exposure are the major factors in the development of motor complications, and most patients with PD experience motor complications, including wearing-OFF and peak-dose dyskinesias, after several years of LD treatment (Fabbri et al 2023). Currently, there is no curative or disease-modifying treatment available for PD. A fluctuating response to medication(s) has been identified as the main concern among PD patients.

Most approved anti-PD medicinal products may be used either in Parkinson's early or advanced (with motor fluctuations) disease: immediate-release (IR) levodopa (LD) + dopa decarboxylase inhibitors (DDCI), anticholinergics, dopamine agonists (DAs), amantadine, monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI). The exceptions are controlled release forms of LD+DDI and catechol-o-methyltransferase inhibitors (COMTI), which are reserved in Parkinson's advanced disease.

No long-acting preparation of LD combining the advantages of IR and ER components in a modifiedrelease (MR) LD-CD oral combination is currently available in the EU market. In 2015, Numient, the first-generation MR oral formulation, was registered through the centralised procedure and withdrawn in 2019 without being commercialised.

Hopledo ( IPX203) is a novel oral MR levodopa-carbidopa multi-particulate capsule formulation, with a proprietary innovative release system to allow better targeting of the active ingredient(s) and a more efficient therapeutic action. The IPX203 capsule has two components: component I contains IR granules and component II ER-coated beads. The IR granules contain 100% of CD dose and 25% of LD dose. The ER part of IPX203 is structured as follows:

- An enteric polymer that prevents the pellets from disintegrating too early in the stomach;

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

- A mucoadhesive polymer designed to keep the ER beads adhered to the area of absorption longer to sustain LD plasma levels. The exact site and duration of absorption are unknown;
- A sustained-release polymer which releases LD slowly;
- A drug core that contains 75% of the total LD dose in a IPX203 capsule. The ER beads do not contain carbidopa.

This formulation was developed and designed to combine a dual-release mechanism and thereby provide fast attainment of therapeutic LD plasma concentrations to ensure early onset of effect and maintain the desired concentrations for a longer duration with minimal peak-to trough-fluctuations than what would be provided by other authorised oral LD-CD products. When administering IPX203, LD from IR granules produces an initial boost of LD exposure, with a rapid onset of effect, followed by continuous LD supply from the ER beads. With a prolonged duration of stable therapeutic concentrations after each dose, IPX203 is designed to achieve better control PD symptoms, fewer motor fluctuations or unfavourable side effects such as dyskinesia, less frequent dosing, enhanced patient's compliance, and possibly improved quality of life in PD patients. Additionally, IPX203 design would allow for dosing intervals of approximately 6-8 hours (TID; range: 2 to 4 times/day) in PD patients with motor fluctuations.

In summary, Hopledo would avoid the limitation of slow initial release and the consequent latency to improvement of motor symptoms seen with controlled-release (CR) formulations.

## 9.2. Main clinical studies

IPX203-B16-02 is a Phase 3, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallelgroup, prospective, multicentre study that evaluated safety and efficacy of IPX203 in comparison to IR LD-CD in the treatment of LD-CD experienced subjects with PD who had motor fluctuations, (despite being) treated with stable regimens of IR LD-CD.

Figure 19: Study IPX203-B16-02 scheme

<!-- image -->

The study had up to 4-week screening period, a 3-week open-label IR CD-LD dose adjustment period, a 4-week open-label period for conversion to IPX203, and a 13-week DB, double-dummy treatment period.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Subjects were randomised in a 1:1 ratio, and stratified by centre, to receive either IPX203 (with matching IR CD-LD placebo) or IR CD-LD (with matching IPX203 placebo). They continued to take permitted non-CD-LD-based PD medications throughout the study, if documented in their pre-study regimen, and if dosing regimens had been stable for at least 4 weeks prior to Visit 1. A 'stable dosing regimen' meant no change in dose or dosing frequency.

On Week 7 at visit four subjects were randomised in 1:1 ratio into one of two DB parallel treatment arms of IPX203 (and matching IR CD-LD placebo) or IR CD-LD (and matching IPX203 placebo).

This pivotal study, with a formulation to be given TID for the treatment of fluctuating PD patients, had an acceptable study design to assess motor control in PD patients.

## 9.3. Favourable effects

IPX203 provided maintenance of effect of the optimised scheduled TID treatment (every 8 hours of daytime) with minimal loss (0.5 h), as compared to IR LD (loss of 1.03 h), in the randomised withdrawal study described above, after previous treatment optimisation. The maintenance of 'Good ON time' was not at the expense of increased 'OFF time' (0.38h, compared to 0.86h with IR LD), nor sleep time. It was further supported by the Patient Global Impression of Change (PGI-C) score where 29.7% of patients felt 'much' or 'very much improved', as compared to 18.8% of patients on IR LD.

## 9.3.1. Uncertainties and limitations about favourable effects

From an efficacy perspective, uncertainties remain regarding the observed 0.53-hour difference between IRLD and IPX203 in patients already benefiting from over 10 hours of 'Good ON' quality on distribution of dyskinesias, among the patients with different levels of improvement in motor fluctuations, and on the results of the performed PEP analysis per subgroups. Notably, the favourable effects are driven by subjects aged &lt;65 years.

The pivotal study IPX203-B16-02 applied sequential open-label run-in phases (IR LD/CD dose adjustment and IPX203 conversion/stabilisation) before randomisation. Consequently, only subjects who tolerated and responded to IPX203 were randomised. This potentially introduced selection bias and impacted validity of the estimated treatment effect. Furthermore, the high dropout rate, particularly the 83 subjects who withdrew during the dose conversion period, might have impacted the efficacy results. However, these discontinuations were mostly due to the transition to IPX203 falling below the patients' expectations (32 out of the 83 subjects who discontinued, while in the IPX203 conversion period, had their reason described). The majority reported that the treatment had failed to meet their expectations in terms of efficacy or symptom control or lack of efficacy (10 subjects) rather than due to AEs.

In general, the impact of these 83 dropouts on the overall efficacy and safety should be interpreted in the context that IPX203 is a new MR formulation designed to replace IR LD-CD in PD patients with motor fluctuations. Conversion to IPX203 involved dose titration, including transient lack of efficacy or dopaminergic AEs, which could lead to discontinuation. The initial suggested IPX203 doses in the protocol were based on average bioavailability relative to IR LD-CD. However, most subjects required individualised up-titration or down-titration to achieve an optimal balance of efficacy and tolerability. During the 4-week IPX203 dose-conversion period, 83 subjects (14.1%) discontinued primarily due to AEs and lack of efficacy. It is agreed that these discontinuations largely reflected the process of establishing a clinically effective and tolerable IPX203 regimen rather than inherent lack of efficacy of IPX203.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Overall, the observed magnitude of effect of IPX203 was small (0.53 hour) as compared to IR-LD, but IPX203 was administered three times a day while IR-LD was to be taken five times a day. The fact that the three oral formulations of IPX203 performed better than the five of IR-LD suggested that the time of intake is less critical for IPX203 than with IR-LD, representing an inherent advantage in the target patient's population, especially elderly patients with moderate-severe motor fluctuations and/or those who cannot handle infusion pumps or are not eligible for deep brain stimulation (DBS) treatment.

## 9.4. Unfavourable effects

In total, 731 participants received IPX203: 589 were enrolled in the pivotal Phase 3 trial and its 9month open-label extension (Study IPX203-B16-03) in PD patients with motor fluctuations, providing the main body of safety data. The adverse event (AE) profile is largely consistent with the known safety profile from other LD/CD formulations. The most common adverse drug reactions (ADRs) were dyskinesia, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness. Most events were mild in severity and their distribution between treatment groups was broadly comparable. In line with the established LD/CD safety profile, the principal identified risks remain dyskinesia, psychosis-related events, impulse control disorders, orthostatic hypotension, somnolence/sudden sleep onset, and neuroleptic malignant syndrome. These are recognised class risks, already addressed through routine SmPC warnings, and do not appear to be increased in frequency or severity with IPX203 compared with other formulations. Melanoma is also retained, in accordance with the class labelling.

## 9.4.1. Uncertainties and limitations about unfavourable effects

Overall, there were no new and unknown safety issues reported during the clinical development programme. However, higher incidence of TEAEs, including serious TEAEs and TEAEs that led to study discontinuation, were observed in subjects receiving IPX203 compared to IR CD-LD, particularly in older participants. The main uncertainties relate to subgroup characterisation of elderly and patients with renal impairment. Exposure in older patients, especially those above 75 years, remains uncharacterised, as no population PK analysis was conducted, no PK data were assessed in the Phase 3 studies, and no patient above 85 years was enrolled in IPX203 clinical trials. In addition, a treatment-related TEAE signal was observed in subjects with stage 3a/3b chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the numbers of Stage 3a/3b subjects CKD were small, which limits, but does not exclude, a relevant risk, given the plausible mechanism. These uncertainties and limitations have been carefully reflected in the product information (PI).

## 9.6. Benefit-risk assessment and discussion

## 9.6.1. Importance of favourable and unfavourable effects

Motor fluctuations and dyskinesias are the most relevant drawbacks in patients with advanced PD. Treatment options may mitigate fluctuations, usually at the cost of less optimal 'Good ON' time, increased 'OFF' time or dyskinesias or added AEs (impulse control disorders with DA, hallucinations, diarrhoea and weight loss with COMTI).

The primary endpoint (PEP) of the pivotal Study IPX203-B16-02 was met. Subjects receiving IPX203 showed an improvement in the mean 'Good ON' time from baseline to the end of the double-blind therapy when compared with those receiving IR CD-LD (IPX203: -0.39 h and IR CD-LD: -0.97 h). IPX203 resulted in more hours of 'Good ON' time compared with IR CD-LD.

Subjects receiving IPX203 showed an improvement in the mean 'OFF' time from baseline to Visit 7/ET when compared with those receiving IR CD-LD (IPX203: 0.29 h and IR CD-LD: 0.76 h).

'OFF' time increased less in the IPX203 group (LS mean: 0.38 h) when compared with IR CD-LD group (LS mean: 0.86 h).

IPX203 treatment resulted in less 'OFF time' compared with IR CD-LD treatment (p=0.0252, difference in LS means: -0.48 h [95% CI: -0.90, -0.06]).

However, in the PP Analysis Set, statistical significance was not reached in the 'Good ON' results. In addition, the pivotal study IPX203-B16-02 applied sequential open-label run-in phases (IR LD/CD dose adjustment and IPX203 conversion/stabilisation) before randomisation. Consequently, only subjects who tolerated and responded to IPX203 were randomised, potentially introducing selection bias and limiting the validity of the estimated treatment effect. The high number of dropouts in study IPX203-B16-02 (especially, the 83 during the dose conversion period of whom 10 due to lack efficacy), might have had a potential impact on efficacy.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

In conclusion, the benefit has been presented with the maintenance of improvement in an optimised fluctuating PD population, with a difference of better 'Good ON' time of 0.53 h in the IPX203 arm as opposed to the IR LD arm, with a smaller but relevant impact in 'OFF' time, given the fact that the 'good ON' time was increased.

Overall, the observed magnitude of effect of IPX203 was small (0.53 hour) as compared to IR-LD, but IPX203 was administered three times a day while IR-LD was to be taken five times a day. The fact that the three oral formulations of IPX203 performed better than the five of IR-LD suggested that the time of intake is less critical for IPX203 than with IR-LD, representing an inherent advantage in the target patient's population, especially for elderly patients with moderate-severe motor fluctuations and/or those who cannot handle infusion pumps or are not eligible for deep brain stimulation (DBS) treatment.

From a safety perspective, the higher incidence of TEAEs, including serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to study discontinuation in IPX203 compared to IR CD-LD group is concentrated in elderly and renally impaired patients. These findings have been carefully addressed throughout the PI.

## 9.6.2. Balance of Benefits and Risks

Levodopa, in a fixed dose combination with a dopa decarboxylase inhibitor (DDI), has been the gold standard for the treatment of PD for over 50 years.

IPX203 is a MR formulation for the treatment of adult patients with Parkinson's disease and moderate to severe motor fluctuations who have not been sufficiently stabilised with oral levodopa/dopa decarboxylase (DDC) inhibitor-based treatment regimens.

The AEs profile of IPX203 is largely consistent with the known safety profile from other levodopa/carbidopa formulations. The most commonly identified ADR were dyskinesia, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness.

## 9.6.3. Additional considerations on the benefit-risk balance

Not applicable.

## 9.7. Benefit-risk conclusions

## 9.7.1. CHMP conclusions

The benefit/risk profile of Hopledo is positive.
